correctness.rationale: For every commutative chain ring R the explicit group splitting reduces internal conjugacy to the equation (t-1)z=(v-1)u. The image of the corresponding R-linear map is the ideal of valuation min(alpha,beta); subtracting the forbidden nonunit multipliers gives centralizer orders U q^alpha or q^(m+beta). The two disjoint valuation cases yield exact class multiplicities and class-number sum. A generating additive character yields a faithful R-module identification of the additive dual; Clifford theory and orbit-stabilizer give every irreducible degree, with squared degrees summing to the group order. Independent exhaustive small-ring direct matrix commutation and dual unit-orbit enumeration reproduce each distribution. Finite examples do not replace the unrestricted proof.

originality.rationale: No source inspected at the statement level gives the complete two-family internal Borel conjugacy-class-size multiset for all commutative finite chain rings. The 2010 and 2012 papers study the ambient general linear group, the 2021 affine enumeration is over finite-field vector spaces, and the 2024 Borel Gelfand-pair work studies induction and constituent multiplicities. The additive-dual orbit observation in the last paper precedes the character-degree companion, which is not claimed as an independently novel technique. A specialized affine-group conjugacy enumeration might still overlap; this remains a genuine priority risk.

value.rationale: Complete class-size multiplicities of a natural finite solvable group are substantially finer than its class number and determine its centralizer statistics and commuting probability. The full simultaneously explicit character-degree spectrum yields complex group-algebra invariance across nonisomorphic chain-ring models of all lengths; the special center jump at q=2 is a sharp structural boundary. This addresses a natural complete invariant for a standard Borel/mirabolic family rather than an arbitrary isolated instance. Risk: the representation-degree portion is a classical-method consequence and does not by itself support novelty or value of the class-size result.
